PullRequest.Title: smoke: include the last polled result in Code.poll timeout errors
PullRequest.Body:
Diagnostics for `SMOKE-SETTINGS-JSON-EDIT-CONTEXT-TIMEOUT`, a new macOS smoke flake in main CI (pipeline 727) run [499214](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=499214). Test-only.

## What failed

The Terminal suite's `decorationsEnabled` test failed in its `beforeEach` hook, inside the shared `SettingsEditor.addUserSettings` helper:

```
Timeout: get editor selection '.monaco-editor[data-uri$="settings.json"] .native-edit-context' after 20 seconds
```

The hook clears `settings.json` to `{}`, saves and closes it, reopens it, clicks line 1 at (1,1), presses Right and waits for the edit-context selection to be `1/1`. Every step up to Right succeeded. Then 28 polls over 20 s never accepted the selection.

It's intermittent. 33 `settings.json` opens ran in the same smoke job, 9 of them on the same close-then-reopen path, and all the others passed on their first poll. Mocha doesn't retry hooks, and official smoke has no fresh-process rerun, so a repeat would fail an official.

## Why this change

`Code.poll` logs `Did not pass accept function` and throws a generic timeout, so the log can't say which selection the editor actually had (for example `2/2` if a restored cursor overwrote the click, or `0/0` if the content wasn't there yet). Without that, any fix would be a guess.

## Change

In `Code.poll`, when the accept function rejects a result, the result is kept as a JSON string, truncated to 500 characters with the full length noted:

- The existing log line becomes `Did not pass accept function, last result: {...}`.
- The thrown timeout error gets ` Last result: {...}` appended, so it also shows in the mocha failure and the CI bot's post. Its existing prefix is unchanged.
- If the last attempt threw instead, nothing is appended, as before.

This applies to every poll-based wait, which gives the same diagnostic to other smoke timeouts too.

## Validation

- `tsc` on `test/automation` and `oxlint` on the changed file are clean.
- I called `poll` with a fake driver:
  - A rejected selection gives `Timeout: get editor selection X after 0 seconds. Last result: {"selectionStart":2,"selectionEnd":2}`.
  - A 2000-character result is cut to 500 with `… (2002 characters)`.
  - A last attempt that throws appends nothing.
  - An accepted result still resolves.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Settings JSON setup and other scalar polling waits (selection, title, text, focus).
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The smoke test awaits a driver result and acceptance before continuing. New result formatting runs synchronously in the Node automation process only after rejection, before the unchanged 100 ms retry delay; accepted results return without formatting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Obtain window.driver with evaluateHandle and evaluate the read in the browser/Electron renderer, returning the selected result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One handle lookup and one renderer evaluation per attempt; getElements returns all matching elements in that evaluation, not a separate IPC per element. No changed call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same renderer calls, result transport and acceptance checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The poll awaits the renderer result before evaluating its predicate.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify the rejected result and retain a diagnostic prefix with a full-length suffix when applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per rejected attempt, never for accepted attempts or driver exceptions; selection payload size is constant.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Rejections assigned a constant error string without formatting the result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New synchronous formatting precedes the retry delay.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selection object containing two numbers per rejected selection attempt; default maximum 200 attempts. Text/title waits scale with returned string length rather than workspace file count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each poll is serial: await read, predicate/format, await delay. No additional polls or parallel driver calls are scheduled by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache or negative cache; every attempt rereads current state. Driver handles are looked up each time, unchanged. Diagnostic state is replaced on rejection and cleared on exception.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added rejection-only serialization and unchanged critical path and boundary counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured timings. Scalar selection results are small; text sizes vary, but inspected settings and ordinary text callers do not establish a large-data trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable regression: selection diagnostic work is small and successful/throwing attempts avoid it entirely.

Scenarios.Scenario: Terminal initialization, output replay, and waits for expected terminal text.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Terminal.waitForTerminalText awaits Code.waitForTerminalBuffer. Each attempt collects and transports the active buffer, tests the predicate, and formats rejected buffers before sleeping. Replay tests wait for sequence 99 before reconnecting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lookup driver, evaluate a renderer read that translates every active xterm buffer line, and transfer one string array.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One handle lookup and one renderer evaluation returning the whole buffer per attempt, independent of line count; collection and transport bytes scale with buffer content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full-buffer collection and transport occurred on every attempt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the rejected buffer array completely before slicing its diagnostic representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional full-array serialization per rejected attempt; no per-line IPC and no formatting on the accepting attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automation-side JSON diagnostic serialization on predicate rejection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Added CPU/allocation on the automation retry path, not in the application renderer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All active buffer lines per attempt. The inspected replay test deliberately produces 100 short sequence lines at 100 ms intervals; other inspected terminal-text tests use short marker output. Default retry limit is 200.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One read at a time per poll, followed by 100 ms sleep. Separate existing waits can overlap, but the diff introduces no concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live buffer is reread without caching to observe output; no positive/negative cache changed. Only the latest diagnostic is referenced, not an accumulated history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in rejection-only additional serialization and its linear payload scaling; insufficient evidence of a realistically costly payload in this test-only path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Full serialization is not work-bounded by the 500-character output limit, but the inspected smoke fixtures establish roughly 100 short lines, not large or sustained scrollback output. No measured CPU/GC or latency degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: Considered repeated full serialization; omitted as a finding because the traced smoke workloads do not establish a substantive performance regression rather than small diagnostic overhead.

Scenarios.Scenario: DOM collection waits for editor groups, terminal teardown/decorations, SCM changes, and completed chat responses.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The caller awaits a matching collection/count or resource. Renderer DOM traversal, element serialization and transfer already precede predicate acceptance; the diff adds diagnostic formatting only for rejected returned collections.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Collect all matching DOM elements in one renderer evaluation, optionally serialize descendants, and transfer the complete collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One handle lookup and one evaluate call per attempt, not per matching row or descendant. Traversal/layout and result transport scale with matched rendered DOM.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same recursive traversal, geometry reads and full-collection transport per attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited read and traversal before the predicate.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON serialization of a rejected element collection for the latest diagnostic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialization per rejected collection, proportional to its complete returned representation; accepted collections are not formatted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Rejection recorded only a constant string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Added synchronous automation-side formatting before another retry.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Matched elements plus descendants for recursive calls, including attributes and descendant text. Inspected terminal editor tests expect one or two groups; SCM/chat queries operate on rendered rows/responses. Empty collections avoid large formatting; Chat Disabled's broad recursive query succeeds as soon as its single root exists.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial per poll. Terminal KillAll's existing Promise.race may leave a poll running after its two-second fallback, but neither that lifetime nor the number of polls was introduced here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No collection cache; each attempt must observe current DOM. Only the most recent diagnostic is replaced; no new long-lived map or listener ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added serialization, rejection guard, grouping and unchanged renderer work/concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rendered collection sizes and rejection durations vary. No evidence that inspected realistic fixtures repeatedly reject heavyweight DOM snapshots sufficient to cause material runner slowdown; pre-existing renderer layout/traversal costs must not be attributed to this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence reportable regression. Do not report the unchanged recursive DOM/layout costs, existing teardown cancellation issue, or hypothetical unbounded collections.

Scenarios.Scenario: Startup/action polling and final timeout reporting.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Action polls and whenWorkbenchRestored use always-accept predicates, so successful driver calls return immediately without new diagnostic work. Exception retries also skip serialization. On timeout, existing logging occurs before the error is thrown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing renderer actions and readiness requests, using driver lookup/evaluation where applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one action/read per attempt; successful always-accept calls do not reach describePollResult. No new subprocess, network or database operations on these poll paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same requests, waits and exception retry scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action/read remains awaited; no new diagnostic work on successful startup/action calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous append of timeout logging through configured FileLogger; driver proxy logging also remains unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same three logger invocations at poll timeout. The existing lastError entry gains a diagnostic prefix of at most 500 characters plus length annotation; no additional append per rejection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same three timeout log calls, with a constant rejection message or last exception stack.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous timeout logging precedes throwing, with only bounded additional diagnostic output.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Default 200 attempts, with caller overrides for some waits. Timeout diagnostics add one capped result representation to an existing log message and thrown error, not a log per rejected attempt.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new initialization, subprocess launch or parallel work; existing serial action retry loops are preserved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changes to readiness caching, action retry state, or logger lifecycle. Last diagnostic is cleared on exceptions and becomes unreachable when the poll completes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from always-accept caller predicates, the early return before formatting, and unchanged logging locations/counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem timing depends on CI environment, but boundary count is unchanged and extra output is small. Static review only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No startup regression or logging fan-out. This PR adds diagnostics, not a demonstrated fix of an existing performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the complete single-file inventory and all four diff hunks against base 72ebe055d56345a7b8c8d611b786c7721f87eb7e. Traced scalar, terminal-buffer, recursive DOM, startup/action and timeout logging paths. Added rejection-only full serialization was considered, but inspected realistic test inputs do not establish a high-confidence substantive regression. No findings or concrete regression-fix provenance signals.
